chore(infra): enable Entra dual-IdP in prod (entra_enabled = true) (#495)

Flips `entra_enabled = true` for prod. Same one-line change as #350 did
for dev, same file shape, different tfvars.

## Why now

Needed to kick off the **2026 data call**. HHS/OpDiv participants
authenticate via Entra — `users.identity_provider` is `okta` for CMS and
`entra` for HHS/OpDivs (migration 0030). With the flag false in prod,
the `/login/entra*` listener rule doesn't exist and
`/api/v1/auth/lookup` falls through to the OIDC-gated `/api/*` rule, so
those users have no login path at all. Every non-CMS participant is
blocked until this flips.

## Scope

One line plus its comment, `infrastructure/tfvars/prod.tfvars`. No code,
no migrations. `dev.tfvars` is untouched (already `true` on main).

## What dev has proven

Dev has run dual-IdP for ~6 weeks. Nothing Entra-related has landed
since #408 on 2026-07-09.

Prod also gets the flip in better shape than dev did — dev was flipped
bare and shook out five follow-ups afterward, all of which are already
on main here:

- #351 — CloudFront `/login/*` behavior to the ALB origin (Entra login
was AccessDenied without it)
- #354 — Okta JWT `kid` validation + key-fetch hardening
- #352 — HHS-wide admins can set `identity_provider` on user create
- #377 — ALB access logs, ELBAuth alarms, backend 401 instrumentation
- #408 — logout clearing app session + both ALB OIDC cookies

## Pre-merge blockers

These are prod-account operational state, not code. Not verifiable from
the repo, so they need confirming before merge. Status and references
updated 2026-07-30.

- [x] **`ztmf_session_signing_key` seeded in prod**
(`scripts/bootstrap-entra-secrets.sh`). An empty key fails session
minting closed (`secrets.tf:37`). Note this breaks **both** IdPs, not
just Entra — post-flip, Okta also routes through `SessionHandler` to
mint the app session cookie. An unseeded key means nobody logs into
prod.
- **Still open.** The container exists but there is no evidence a value
was written. The 2026-06-15 15:03:20Z timestamp on both secrets falls
inside #341's merge-triggered PROD `terraform apply` (15:03:03Z to
15:05:50Z), so it records container creation, not seeding. No workflow
invokes the bootstrap script, so CI cannot have written them. Settling
this needs `LastChangedDate` against `CreatedDate`, or CloudTrail
`PutSecretValue`, neither of which is reachable from a human credential.
The script generates this key itself, so no external input is required
to close it.
- [x] **`ztmf_entra_oidc` seeded in prod.** Terraform reads this one at
plan time (`data.tf:74`), so an unseeded secret fails the apply rather
than breaking at runtime.
- **Still open**, same evidence as above. Closing it needs tenant id,
client id and client secret from the Entra tenant owners.
- [ ] **Entra app registration has the prod redirect URI** and prod
users are **assigned to the app**. Flagging specifically because of the
AADSTS50105 (user-not-assigned) hit on dev on 2026-06-30 — and per the
scope note in `monitoring-login-auth.tf:12-16`, the ELBAuth alarms
*cannot* catch that class. Entra rejects it before any callback, so no
datapoint is ever emitted. It's the most likely first failure on a fresh
prod tenant and it will be silent.
- **Still open, and the only item that is not ours to close.** The URI
needed is `https://ztmf.cms.gov/oauth2/idpresponse`. Also worth settling
in the same conversation: whether prod gets its own app registration
rather than sharing dev's, since sharing means one client secret spans
both environments and stops `AUTH_ENTRA_AUDIENCE` distinguishing them.
- [x] **Decide login alarm routing for prod.**
`alarm_notification_email` is unset in `prod.tfvars`, and
`monitoring-login-auth.tf:31` count-gates the SNS subscription on a
non-empty string — so prod gets the topic and the alarms with **zero
subscribers**. Dev's `jono@aquia.us` is flagged in its own comment as an
interim individual address to be replaced before prod. Deliberately left
out of this PR since it needs a real destination decision (shared inbox
or Slack webhook); happy to fold it in here or take it as a follow-up.
- **Done, #496.** Both dev and prod now route to
`ISPGZeroTrust@cms.hhs.gov`, which also de-personalises dev. Applied,
and both SNS subscriptions confirmed rather than left pending.

### Found during review and fixed ahead of this PR

- **#497** — the session cookie is now host-only. `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN`
resolved to the bare apex in prod, so this flip would have handed a live
prod session cookie to the dev and impl hostnames. Merged and deployed
ahead of this PR, so the condition is prevented rather than remediated.
Detail in CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#257 (closed).
- **#498** — `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` renamed to `AUTH_ORIGIN_HOST`, since
after #497 it only feeds the same-origin check.

Tracked separately, neither gating this PR: CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#258
(cross-environment cookie check, blocked *on* this PR) and
CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#259 (session tokens are unbound bearer
credentials with no revocation path).

## Deploy behavior

Nothing applies while this is open, draft or not.
`orchestration-prod.yml` triggers only on `pull_request: closed` +
merged. `orchestration-dev.yml` does run on the open PR, but it applies
with `dev.tfvars`, so it can't exercise this change — there's no
pre-merge plan output for prod. **Merging is the deploy.**

The flag swap is destroy-and-create in a single apply: the two Okta
rules (priorities 1-2) are destroyed and the four dual-IdP rules
created, so priorities never collide. `moved` blocks in
`alb-internal.tf:127-135` keep the un-indexed addresses from churning.

Worth having someone on a prod Okta login the moment it applies —
priority 4 takes the ALB out of the `/api/*` auth path and hands the
gate to the backend session cookie, which is the highest-consequence
part of the change.

Refs #341, #350

commits.message:
chore(auth): rename AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN to reflect its only use (#498)

`config.Auth.CookieDomain`, bound to `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN`, used to do
two unrelated jobs. It supplied the session cookie's `Domain` attribute,
and it is the host `sameOrigin` expects to see in the `Origin` (then
`Referer`) header of a state-changing request. #497 removed `Domain`
from both `SetSessionCookie` and `ClearSessionCookie`, so no code path
sets a cookie domain any more and the same-origin check is the field's
only remaining consumer.

That leaves the name describing a job the value no longer does, which is
a trap of its own. Someone setting a variable called
`AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN` would reasonably expect it to scope the session
cookie, and it does not. This renames the field to `OriginHost` and the
environment variable to `AUTH_ORIGIN_HOST`, and rewrites the doc comment
to describe the same-origin check it actually feeds, including the
fallback to the request `Host` when the value is empty.

This is a pure rename. `sameOrigin` reads the same value, compares it
the same way, and falls back the same way. Terraform still injects
`local.domain_name`, only under the new name, because the public
hostname is exactly what a browser puts in `Origin` and therefore
exactly what the check should expect.

#497 described the follow-up as splitting the field into a cookie-domain
setting plus an Origin-check setting named for its purpose. This does
the rename half and deliberately skips the other half. After #497 there
is no code path that reads a cookie domain, so a new
`AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN` would be either dead configuration or, the
moment something started reading it, a re-armed version of the
over-scoping #497 removed. Host-only scoping is the behaviour we want in
every environment, and the way to get it is to have no field for it at
all. Renaming the surviving field is what actually closes the root
cause, since the root cause was one name standing for two things.

#497 left the field alone specifically because clearing or renaming it
could start failing the Origin check behind CloudFront, and that is the
part of this change worth checking rather than the rename itself. It is
settled below.

## Deploy atomicity

An environment variable rename couples the task-definition change to the
image rollout. If Terraform injected `AUTH_ORIGIN_HOST` while the
running image still read `AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN`, `sameOrigin` would
silently fall back to `r.Host` for the duration of the gap, and behind
CloudFront that is not guaranteed to be the public hostname. The two
land together, in the same ECS task definition revision, so no such gap
exists.

`.github/workflows/orchestration-prod.yml` runs `analysis`, then
`backend`, then `infrastructure`, and the `infrastructure` job declares
`needs: [analysis, backend]`, so `terraform apply` cannot start until
the backend job has succeeded. `.github/workflows/backend.yml` pushes
the image tagged with the short commit SHA, then writes that same SHA to
the image-pointer SSM parameter with `aws ssm put-parameter
--overwrite`, and closes with the comment "Deployment of the latest
image will happen with terraform apply during infrastructure deploy".
`.github/workflows/infrastructure.yml` then checks out the merge commit
and runs `terraform apply`, which reads that pointer through `data
"aws_ssm_parameter" "ztmf_api_tag"` in `infrastructure/data.tf` and so
sees the tag the backend job just wrote.

The two changes are attributes of one resource. `infrastructure/ecs.tf`
sets `aws_ecs_task_definition.ztmf_api`'s `image` from that data source,
and builds the container's `environment` as `concat([...],
local.entra_api_env)`, which is where the renamed variable lives. A
single apply produces a single new revision carrying both the new image
and the new variable name, so there is no revision in which the new
variable name meets an image that reads the old one, and none in which
the new image meets the old variable name. `orchestration-dev.yml` gates
its backend job on a backend diff and this PR changes Go files, so the
dev deploy builds and rolls out a new image the same way.

A bare rename is therefore safe and no back-compat fallback is needed.
As a secondary point, the `/api/*` CloudFront behaviour forwards
`headers = ["*"]`, so even the fallback path would most likely resolve
to the viewer's host, but naming the expected host explicitly is still
right, because the check should not depend on header-forwarding
configuration staying as it is.

## Note on the test setup that goes away

Two call sites in `session_test.go` set `CookieDomain` to a non-empty
value before asserting the cookie stayed host-only, because the field
used to be the one thing that could have leaked a `Domain`, and #497
needed that setup to keep the assertion from passing vacuously. No
configuration can feed the cookie's `Domain` now, so the setup has
nothing to prove and it is removed. The host-only assertions stay as the
guard against reintroducing a `Domain`. They are weaker than they were,
in that they can no longer be driven by a config value, and there is no
way to keep that strength without keeping a cookie-domain field, which
is the thing this change is removing the last trace of.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...` clean
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `go test -short ./...` green, 577 tests across 19 packages
- [x] `TestSameOrigin` passes all six subtests unchanged, confirming the
fallback-to-`Host` path behaves the same
- [x] `TestSetSessionCookie_Attributes` and
`TestClearSessionCookie_Attributes` still assert the cookie is issued
host-only
- [x] `terraform fmt -check -recursive` clean in `infrastructure/`
- [x] `gofmt` clean on the lines this change touches. `middleware.go`
carries one pre-existing alignment nit on an unrelated const block that
`gofmt` also reports against `main`, left alone to keep this diff to the
rename
- [x] `git grep -n 'CookieDomain\|AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN'` returns nothing
- [ ] After the rollout, confirm a state-changing request from the
browser still succeeds, which is what exercises `sameOrigin` against the
injected `AUTH_ORIGIN_HOST`

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#257. This completes that ticket's code
cleanup. Its remaining post-rollout verification stays open.

commits.message:
fix(auth): scope the session cookie to the issuing host (#497)

The session cookie now omits the `Domain` attribute, so the browser
scopes it to the exact host that issued it. Both cookie setters
previously copied the configured cookie domain onto `Domain`, and per
RFC 6265 an explicit `Domain` scopes a cookie to that domain and to
every subdomain beneath it. The prod hostname is the bare apex, so a
prod session would be delivered to the dev and impl hostnames as well,
and to any subdomain added later. Omitting the attribute is what
produces host-only scoping, which keeps the credential confined to the
environment that minted it.

Go's `net/http` gives us exactly that with no extra work:
`Cookie.String()`, which `http.SetCookie` calls, writes `; Domain=` only
when the field is non-empty, so an unset `Domain` is absent from the
serialized `Set-Cookie` header rather than emitted empty.

`sameOrigin` in `backend/cmd/api/internal/auth/middleware.go` is
deliberately untouched, and that is the part worth checking. It reads
the same `Auth.CookieDomain` value as the expected `Origin` host and
falls back to the request `Host` when the field is empty. Behind
CloudFront with a VPC origin to the internal ALB, the `Host` the
container observes is not necessarily the public hostname, so clearing
or renaming the field could start failing the Origin check on every
state-changing request. This change therefore leaves the config field,
its env binding and the Origin-check path exactly as they were, and only
stops putting the value on the cookie. Splitting the overloaded field
into a separate cookie-domain setting plus an Origin-check setting named
for its actual purpose is a deliberate follow-up, still outstanding.

Both setters change in the same commit because they are coupled. A
browser only removes a cookie when the expiring cookie's `Domain`
matches the one it was stored with, so dropping `Domain` from
`SetSessionCookie` alone would leave `ClearSessionCookie` unable to
clear the session. That failure mode passes a casual test, since login
and normal browsing look fine and only logout silently stops working.

## Test plan

- [x] `TestSetSessionCookie_Attributes` asserts the issued cookie
carries no `Domain`, so a future change cannot silently re-widen it. The
test sets `Auth.CookieDomain` to a non-empty value first, because it is
empty in the test environment and the assertion would otherwise pass no
matter what the setter does.
- [x] `TestClearSessionCookie_Attributes` asserts the logout cookie is
emptied, expired, and also carries no `Domain`, covering the
coupled-setter trap.
- [x] Both new assertions were confirmed to fail when `Domain` is
reintroduced, so they are load-bearing rather than vacuous.
- [x] `go build ./...` clean.
- [x] `go vet ./...` clean.
- [x] `go test -short ./...` fully green across all 19 packages.
- [x] `go test ./...` green except the pre-existing integration tests,
which need a live database and fail the same way on `main` without one.
`cmd/api/internal/auth` passes.
- [x] `gofmt` clean on both changed files. The repo carries no
golangci-lint config; the only lint gates are terraform fmt and tflint
for infrastructure and the Redocly OpenAPI lint, none of which this
change touches.
- [ ] Manual check that no unit test can cover: sign in to prod first,
then to a lower environment, in one browser profile, and confirm the
lower environment works. That ordering is the one that breaks while the
cookie is apex-scoped.

## Deploy note

A session issued before this change is a distinct cookie from the
host-only one, so the new expiry does not delete it. Only dev is in that
state, because `entra_enabled` gates the variable and it is true only in
dev, where the configured value is dev's own leaf hostname. The effect
there is bounded: `r.Cookie` returns the older of two same-named
cookies, so a dev browser holding a pre-deploy cookie keeps presenting
it and logout does not end that session until the 3 hour `MaxAge`
elapses. It self-heals, and clearing site cookies ends it immediately.
No prod session is involved, since prod sets no cookie domain today and
so holds nothing domain-scoped. Emitting an extra legacy domain-scoped
expiry would close that window, but it would put an apex `Domain` back
on the wire for every prod logout once #495 lands, and leave a dead
dependency on a field the planned split is going to rename, so this
leaves it out. Worth a cookie clear if a dev logout looks sticky just
after this deploys.

## Blockers

This is one of two prerequisites for merging #495, which enables Entra
dual-IdP in prod. Merging #495 is the deploy that applies the flag and
injects the cookie domain into the API task, so merging it is what turns
the over-scoping on. Please do not apply `entra_enabled = true` in prod
until this is in.

The second prerequisite is the config-field split described above. That
work is outstanding, so this PR does not close the tracking ticket.

Refs #495
Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#257

spec drift that today only surfaces in CI and costs a review round-trip

commits.message:
feat(#609, #610): cross-navigation between System Info and the Questionnaire (#640)

* feat(#609, #610): cross-navigation between System Info and the Questionnaire

The two pages were only reachable from the dashboard, so moving between a
system's detail page and its questionnaire meant going back and finding the
system again. The routes are keyed on different identifiers (questionnaire on
:fismaacronym, detail on :fismasystemid) and each page already holds both, so
neither direction needs new lookups to build its link.

System Info gains a Questionnaire button next to Edit, targeting
/questionnaire/<acronym> with no route state: an absent location.state
datacallid is what lets QuestionnairePage resolve the cycle itself, and it keeps
the target a plain shareable URL matching the dashboard's own questionnaire
action. Decommissioned systems link too, leaving the questionnaire's existing
"no questionnaire is available" alert to explain the outcome. The button is
suppressed in edit mode so a dirty form keeps Save/Cancel as its only actions.

The questionnaire header gains System Info and Pillar Scores beside the existing
Compare Datacalls button. Pillar Scores reuses PillarScoresModal, which takes
its rows as a prop rather than fetching, so the handler makes the same
/scores/aggregate call the dashboard action makes and opens on success; a
failure notifies instead of opening an empty modal that would read as "this
system has no scores". System Info carries the same hasSystemAccess gate the
dashboard puts on its System Details action so the two move together if that
access narrows. The selected-data-call fallback chain is now one const, since
both header modals need it.

* fix(#609, #610): address review — flush drafts on unmount, link semantics, no-questionnaire return

Review feedback from @costacalvin on #640.

Blocker: the debounced draft save (1s) had its timer cancelled by the effect
cleanup on unmount, and beforeunload does not fire on in-app navigation, so an
edit made inside the debounce window was dropped when the questionnaire
unmounted. Fixed at the unmount boundary rather than inside the System Info
handler, because the page was already reachable-to-leave via the Dashboard
breadcrumb (BreadCrumbs renders a router Link to "/") and the browser back
button; a handler-level flush would have covered only the new button. A
pendingDraftRef mirrors the payload the debounced save would write, carrying the
save generation, and a mount-once effect flushes it on teardown, skipping when
the generation has moved so a flush cannot resurrect a draft clearCurrentDraft
deleted. saveDraft takes only primitives and touches no component state, so the
write completes after teardown. Verified end to end against the dev stack: type a
note, leave for System Info immediately, return, draft restored.

The no-questionnaire branch returned before the action header, so a
decommissioned or out-of-scope system reached from the new #609 button was a
one-way trip. The System Info link is now shared between that branch and the
main header.

Both cross-navigation controls are real links instead of onClick + navigate, so
open-in-new-tab and copy-link work. The questionnaire side uses MUI Button with
component={RouterLink}, matching the pattern in BreadCrumbs. CmsButton has no
polymorphic component prop, so the System Info side takes href={useHref(path)},
which resolves the same way Link would rather than hand-writing the fragment
(confirmed as #/questionnaire/ssd-ex under the app's hash router).

Also guards the aggregate envelope with res.data?.data ?? [].

Tests: the redundant decommissioned case asserted the same thing as the
lowercased-acronym case, so it is replaced by coverage of the no-questionnaire
return link. Header assertions now check the rendered anchor href. New test for
the unmount flush, confirmed to fail without the fix.

* fix(#609, #610): clear the pending draft by identity, not generation

Race found in #640 review: edits in one session share a generation
(saveGenRef only moves on explicit clears), so when edit A's debounced
save was in flight and edit B replaced the pending payload, save A's
completion cleared the ref that held B. An unmount before B's own
debounce then flushed nothing and B was silently lost. The clear also
ran before the saved check, so a failed write discarded the payload the
unmount flush would have retried.

The completion handler now captures the exact payload object it wrote
and clears the ref only when that write succeeded and the ref still
holds that same object. A newer edit installs a different object, so an
older save's completion can no longer clear it, and a failed write
stays pending for the unmount flush.

Regression test follows the review's sequence exactly: save A starts
and is held unresolved, edit B lands, A resolves, the page unmounts
before B's debounce, and the flush must persist B. It fails against the
previous head with only saveDraft(A) recorded.

The Average System Score tile summed per-system scores only for systems with

systems. Systems with no answers dragged the mean below the scale minimum

computed in the same loop as the numerator so both always cover the same set.

Replace the Total Systems tile with a "Scored / Total Systems" ratio so the

Add a StatisticsBlocks test suite covering the subset-participation case, the
average-between-bounds invariant, and the empty-selection edge case.

Closes #633

commits.message:
Distinguish inferred passes from observed ones in the Insights panel (#632)

fix(insights): distinguish inferred passes from observed ones

SecurityHub's feed carries only FAILED records, so `sechub_passing` is
derived upstream as "mapped control with no active failure". That cannot
tell "evaluated and passed" apart from "never scanned", and a passing
entry is not display-only: rollupControls counts every `{source}_passing`
entry as `satisfied` evidence in the ARS control union. A partially
scanned system would therefore show controls as met on the strength of
checks that never ran.

Mark such sources in INFERRED_PASS_SOURCES. Their entries still render as
green chips, since the check is not failing, but the block summary, the
chip hover, the accessible name, and the collapse toggle all say the
checks reported no findings rather than claiming a pass, and the entries
are withheld from the control rollup.

Removing a source from the set is all that is needed once its feed emits
real passes.

commits.message:
Name the check in plain language on Insights control chip hovers (#631)

* fix(insights): name the check in plain language on control chip hovers

A control chip is labeled with the control id, so its hover was the only
place naming the check behind it — and it named it by slug alone
("Kion · account-without-compliant-password-policy · failed"), leaving the
reader to decode it. The check chips have carried the human sentence since
they were introduced; the control chips never did.

Carry each check's description onto its control evidence and render it
under the slug line, with the same sentence folded into the accessible
name so screen readers get what the hover shows. Covers all three finding
sources, passing and failing; CFACTS evidence has no per-check text and
stays as-is.

* fix(insights): drop the evidence sentence when it repeats the check name

A finding carrying only a title resolves both the check name and the
sentence to that same string, so the control hover printed it twice and
the accessible name announced it twice.

Render extended metadata fields as validated selects (rehome of #626) (#628)

* feat(systems): render extended metadata fields as validated selects (#460)

The extended system-metadata fields (`fips`, `system_type`, `hva`, `cloud_system`, `cloud_service_model`, `goco_coco_gogo`, `system_operator`, `legacy`) rendered as free text, letting dirty values back in. Render them as selects driven by the canonical vocabulary in both the Add/Edit modal and the system detail edit view; `cloud_service_model` is a multi-select stored as a sorted slash-joined combo. Legacy/unmapped values stay visible and valid on an untouched save, and optional fields can be cleared.

The vocabulary is served locally by `src/utils/systemMetadataVocab.ts` as a stopgap: the canonical set is agreed (`ztmf#395`) but the backend vocabulary endpoint (`ztmf#433`) is not built yet. That module is the single swap point: when the endpoint ships, only `fetchSystemMetadataVocab` changes.

* rework(HHS metadata): Applying feedback to cover the actual changes of the BE and the handoff

* feat(system metadata): Stack the fields in the contact card

* fix(systems): hide cloud fields in read view when cloud_system is No (#460)

Match the edit view, which already hides cloud_service_model and cloud_vendor
when cloud_system is No; they are empty in that case anyway.

Backfill the coverage the optional-select bug slipped through:
- optional selects stay out of the error state on a valid form, using a realistic formValid rather than an all-valid stand-in
- clearing an enum select in the modal saves '' not null, and an untouched save omits extended fields (new EditSystemModal test file)
- read-view cross-field hide

* feat(hhs metadata): stack contact fiels in view mode.

* feat(hhs metadata): reframe legacy field as a funding disposition

Rename "Legacy" to "Not Funded for Remediation". It is a self-reported funding disposition, not a statement about age or technology, and "Legacy" read as old tech to every viewer.

- Add a generic optional `helpText` on `FieldConfig`, rendered under the control in both edit surfaces; `legacy` carries the disposition copy.
- Add `booleanLabels` so `legacy` reads Not funded / Funded / Unknown instead of Yes / No against a negative label (`hva` and `cloud_system` keep Yes/No); applied to the edit controls and the read-view text.
- Drop `SystemAttribute.description`: the vocab endpoint stays a plain allowed-values list, help copy lives in the UI.

* fix(hhs metadata): clear free-text modal fields with '' not null

The Add/Edit modal's text branch sent `e.target.value || null`, so clearing `cloud_vendor`, `system_owner`, or `system_owner_email` (email falls through this branch) stored `null`. commits.message:
ZTMF Insights: reorder drawer, alignment disclaimer, failing-first chips, collapse large blocks (#615)

* feat(insights): reorder drawer, alignment disclaimer, failing-first chips, collapse large blocks

Follow-up to the insights rework, focused on how the drawer reads and scales.

- Reorder the drawer: "Based on" now leads, followed by the CFACTS reasoning and
  the per-source sections, with the control-union section moved to the bottom.
- Relabel the control-union section to "Aligns with ARS Controls:" and drop the
  "N of M satisfied" count. The union denominator is not the official ARS total,
  so the count read as a smaller, misleading figure to a CMS reviewer; the chips
  still carry each control's state.
- Add a disclaimer on that section (info button, keyboard reachable): alignment
  maps automated evidence to ARS controls and is not an assessed control
  satisfaction determination. CFACTS remains the system of record for control
  status.
- Order failing chips first in every block so problems sit at the top, and roll
  the passing bulk behind a "Show all N passing checks" toggle once it exceeds a
  couple of rows (mainly Hardenize, which can carry 30+ passing checks). Failing
  findings are always shown and never collapsed.

Expands the panel tests to cover the reorder, the dropped count, the disclaimer,
failing-first ordering, and the collapse toggle.

* fix(insights): restore remediation in chip hovers, fix info-button a11y, reset collapse per question

Addresses the review on the drawer reorder, plus a regression reported on the
Kion chips.

Remediation was unreachable on chip sources. The earlier switch from the
verbose FindingRow card to compact chips left FindingRow rendering only for
Hardenize, so the "How to fix" text that card carried disappeared for Kion and
SecurityHub. The chip hover showed only the dictionary description, which for
some checks is a bare label — account-without-compliant-password-policy reads
"Password Policy", with the actual explanation sitting in remediation. Put it
back in the chip hover and in the accessible name, behind the same
INSIGHTS_SUGGEST_FIX_ENABLED flag FindingRow uses.

Review items:

- The ARS alignment info icon was not in the accessibility tree. SvgIcon
  defaults to aria-hidden when no titleAccess is passed, so its role and name
  were ignored. Un-hide it, and move the full disclaimer into the accessible
  name: MUI Tooltip lets the child's own aria-label win, so the tooltip was
  never wired up as a description and the text was sighted-only.
- Raise the icon's contrast from #8a94a6 (2.91:1 on the panel) to #5c636a
  (5.79:1), clearing the 3:1 non-text minimum in WCAG 1.4.11.
- Reset the passing-checks collapse when the payload changes. The panel and the
  block keep the same React key across a question change, so an expanded block
  stayed expanded on the next question without a click. Reset off the rendered
  check set rather than a question id, since the payload carries no question
  identity and keying the panel would also reset the drawer's open state, which
  is a separate pre-existing issue.
- Drop the redundant index from the ARS chip key; the rollup already dedupes by
  control id.

Tests: remediation reachable in both the hover and the accessible name (and
gone when the flag is off), the info icon queried by role so an aria-hidden
regression fails, a rerender with a changed payload covering the collapse
reset, the drawer order asserted through the middle rather than just the
bookends, and failing-first on the ARS control union.

* fix(deps): bump react-router and react-router-dom to 7.18.0

Three high-severity advisories were published against react-router 7.16.0 in
the last two days, so the snyk dependency scan now fails on every open PR:

- Cross-site Scripting, SNYK-JS-REACTROUTER-18313128
- Open Redirect, SNYK-JS-REACTROUTER-18313144
- Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity, SNYK-JS-REACTROUTER-18313148

Both packages were pinned exact and had drifted apart (react-router 7.16.0
direct, plus a second copy at 7.15.0 pulled in through react-router-dom
7.15.0), so all three showed up on two vulnerable paths each. Moving both to
7.18.0 is the upgrade snyk names as the fix and collapses them back to a single
resolution.

The scan failing is not cosmetic: Analysis gates the ui Deploy job, so a failed
snyk test skips the deploy, and main requires a dev deployment to merge.

Checked the 7.16 to 7.18 changes against this app. The reverse-proxy CSRF and
origin-validation fix applies to the server adapters, which a Vite SPA does not
use; there is no useNavigation call to hit the discriminated-union type change;
and no future flags are set, so the trailingSlashAwareDataRequests rename is not
in play. Typecheck, lint, the full test suite, and a production build all pass.

* fix(insights): never suggest a fix for a passing check, split the disclaimer name from its description

Follow-up review pass on the previous commit.

Remediation was leaking onto passing checks. The "How to fix" text added to the
chip hover and accessible name was not gated on pass/fail, so a passing entry
carrying remediation would tell a reviewer how to fix a check that passed —
wrong guidance in a compliance tool, and on Hardenize it would have put a full
remediation paragraph on each of 30-plus focusable passing chips. The pipeline
does not emit remediation on passing entries today (none of the 4,685 current
ones carry it), so this was latent, but InsightFinding permits it and the guard
belongs on the render path. Same call the passing arrays already make for
severity: a pass is not a severity event, and it is not something to fix.

The ARS alignment disclaimer is now a description rather than part of the name.
Putting all 240 characters in aria-label made for a ~260 character accessible
name, and left the tooltip's own text orphaned in the accessibility tree where a
virtual cursor could reach it a second time. Tooltip's describeChild wires the
disclaimer as aria-describedby instead, so the name stays "About ARS alignment"
and the prose is the description. The title is passed as a node rather than a
string on purpose: with a string, Tooltip also sets a native title attribute and
the browser draws a second tooltip over ours.

The collapse reset now keys off the real question id instead of a signature built
from the rendered check ids. The old signature aliased in the case that matters
most — the same check maps to several questions, so identical ids meant no reset
and the block came up pre-expanded, which is the leak this was meant to fix. It
also could not tell a pass/fail split apart, and collapsed findings with missing
ids to indistinguishable empty strings. InsightPayload has no question identity,
but the page that renders the panel does, so it is threaded through as a prop.
Applied during render rather than in an effect, so the next question does not
paint expanded for a frame and aria-expanded does not flip after paint.

Tests: remediation withheld from a passing chip that carries it, the disclaimer
name asserted short with the prose excluded, the collapse reset covered for a
question change that shares an identical check set, and a same-question rerender
asserted not to collapse what the user opened. The reorder test now selects each
section heading by the rollup summary beside it instead of by DOM position.

Polish the System Delegates section on the FISMA system detail page and update the OpDiv delegate toggle label accessibility.

- **Delegate section UX & terminology:** Rename the new-person flow from "invite" to "provision" to accurately reflect direct account creation with no outgoing email. The candidate search only re-ran on systemId/input changes, so removing a delegate left them missing from the picker until a page reload, and an attached one lingered. Key it off a roster-version counter instead, since eligibility excludes anyone already on the system. A counter rather than the delegates array so the refresh does not depend on referential identity.

Also render the roster's Active / Expiring soon / Expired chip on picker options, reading the access_expires_at the candidate endpoint already returns, so a lapsed candidate is obvious before attaching (attaching one is allowed but still needs a renew to grant access).

Review follow-up on top of Onix Tarrats Calderon's system-delegates commits:
the add call opts out of the global auth interceptor (skipAuthHandling) so the
capability-off 403 reaches the component, and classifyAddError keys on the
DELEGATE_NOT_ENABLED code (paired backend change) rather than a bare 403 the
interceptor would otherwise swallow into a generic toast. Test updated to assert
the coded rejection.

ZTMF Insights: finding-name chips, cross-source ARS control union, per-source sections (#612)

feat(insights): finding-name chips, cross-source ARS control union, per-source sections

Rework the ZTMF Insights drawer so every evidence source reads consistently and
every scored source chip has a matching section explaining it.

Findings as chips:
- Kion and SecurityHub findings now render as compact pass/fail chips labeled by
  the finding name, with description, mapped control, severity, and met/failed
  state in the hover. SecurityHub collapses from multiple rows to one block.
- Hardenize renders a section whenever it has data: failing findings as rows with
  affected domains, a "scanned clean" line when clean, or a pass/fail chip block
  once its passing array ships. Affected domains also ride along in the chip hover.

ARS Controls as a cross-source union:
- The ARS Controls section is now the union of every control any source touches
  (CFACTS coverage plus each Kion/SecurityHub/Hardenize check's mapped control),
  rolled up weakest-link (failing over satisfied over not-satisfied). A control
  that one source passes and another fails is flagged as a conflict and rendered
  as an amber chip whose hover names each source and states how it resolved.

Source model:
- ARS is treated as the control catalog (the ARS Controls section), not an
  evidence source, so the standalone ARS chip is dropped and its coverage rolls up
  under CFACTS, which is the source that assesses it.
- Chip order and drawer section order are aligned (CFACTS, Hardenize, SecurityHub,
  Kion), and "Based on" is derived from the active source chips.

Adds rollupControls with unit tests and expands the panel tests to cover the chip
flip, the control union, conflict handling, and per-source sections.
